sentence: This project builds a model that predicts the risk of oral health complications in people with xerostomia, using clinical informatics methods.
This project uses a single-cell screen to find small molecules that help the immune system target glioblastoma cells for destruction.
This project builds software that reads heart ultrasound images to find heart attack patients at high risk of complications.
This project builds a method that measures DNA methylation clocks and studies how they change with age in mouse muscle.
This project provides shared methods for animal radiotherapy and improves the accuracy of small animal irradiation.
This project uses computational genomics and machine learning to study gene programs and cell signaling pathways in a disease with several distinct forms.
This project builds systems biology models of signaling between tumor cells and immune cells, and looks for drugs that block that signaling.
This project studies how epithelial stem cells sense and adapt to inflammation, and how this helps wound repair.
This project studies how mitochondria and small molecules control stem cell division and fate in Arabidopsis thaliana.
This project develops simplified sequencing workflows to detect drug-resistant tuberculosis early so patients can get appropriate treatment.
This project supports research into the causes, treatment and prevention of diabetes and its complications.
This project tries to find out how methylation of two histone residues guides stem cells as they become different cell types.
This project builds a computational platform that combines behavior and neural data from different labs to study how the nervous system encodes sensation and action.
This project studies how mu opioid receptors are regulated and work at primary cilia on neurons.
This project develops spectral Cherenkov imaging as a real-time tool to measure radiation dose during radiation therapy.
This project studies the structure of the transition state where broadly neutralizing antibodies meet HIV-1 antigen and designs immunogens using artificial intelligence.
This project uses eye imaging and vision tests in animal models of eye diseases to track changes in the visual system.
This project tries to find what drives mutant gliomas to progress and which therapeutic targets could slow this.
This project studies how the inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 drives early muscle wasting and tests whether blocking monocyte and macrophage activation reduces it.
This project builds data methods and an artificial intelligence pipeline to predict drug targets and small molecules for Alzheimer's disease.
